# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 51

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 11

---

## Disagreement 1 — 51:1 "thinking about" vs. "meditating on"

- **EMET:** "I am thinking about the elm tree and the vine"
- **LOGOS:** "I am thinking about / meditating on the elm and the vine"
- **PNEUMA:** "I'm looking at the elm tree and the grapevine and thinking about them"
- **Greek:** *enthumoumai* — to think on, ponder, reflect, meditate
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "I am meditating on the elm and the vine" (LOGOS). *Enthumeomai* suggests deeper reflection than casual "thinking about."

---

## Disagreement 2 — 51:2 "type" vs. "picture" vs. "representation"

- **EMET:** "appointed as a type for the servants of God"
- **LOGOS:** "set forth as a type for the servants of God"
- **PNEUMA:** "set up as a picture for God's servants"
- **Greek:** *typos keitai tois doulois tou theou* — a type/model is laid down for the servants of God
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "set forth as a type for the servants of God" (LOGOS). "Type" is the standard technical term from typological hermeneutics; "picture" (PNEUMA) loses the theological precision.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 51:3 "fastened" vs. "attached"

- **EMET:** "when the vine is fastened upon the elm"
- **LOGOS:** "when the vine is attached to the elm"
- **PNEUMA:** "when the vine wraps itself around the elm"
- **Greek:** *haptomenē tēs pteleas* — clinging to/touching/attached to the elm
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "when the vine is attached to the elm" (LOGOS). "Attached" is more natural; "fastened" implies external binding; PNEUMA's "wraps itself" adds motion not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 51:4 "gives much fruit" vs. "yields much fruit"

- **EMET:** "the elm also gives much fruit"
- **LOGOS:** "the elm also yields much fruit"
- **PNEUMA:** "the elm actually produces a great deal of fruit"
- **Greek:** *pollous karpous dīdōsin* — gives/yields many fruits
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "yields much fruit" (LOGOS). "Yield" is the standard agricultural term in English; "gives" is too generic.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 51:4 "rotten" vs. "rotting"

- **EMET:** "and that rotten"
- **LOGOS:** "and that is rotten"
- **PNEUMA:** "and rotten fruit"
- **Greek:** *sēpomenous* — rotting, spoiling (present participle)
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "and that is rotten." The participle suggests ongoing rot; all three render this adequately.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 51:5 "poor toward the Lord" — all agree on substance

- **EMET:** "is poor toward the Lord"
- **LOGOS:** "is poor toward the Lord"
- **PNEUMA:** "is spiritually impoverished before God"
- **Greek:** *ptōchos tou kyriou* — poor of/toward the Lord
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "is poor toward the Lord" (EMET/LOGOS). PNEUMA adds "spiritually" which is an interpretive gloss; the paradox of a rich person who is poor should be preserved starkly.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 51:5 "without wavering" vs. "without hesitation"

- **EMET:** "supplies all things to the poor man without wavering"
- **LOGOS:** "supplies all things to the poor man without hesitation"
- **PNEUMA:** "gives freely and generously to the poor person"
- **Greek:** *adistaktōs* — without doubting/wavering/hesitating
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "without hesitation" (LOGOS). "Hesitation" captures the economic/practical dimension better than "wavering" which suggests doctrinal doubt.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 51:6 "cannot pray" vs. "cannot pray effectively"

- **EMET:** "the rich man is not able to pray"
- **LOGOS:** "the rich man cannot pray effectively"
- **PNEUMA:** "the rich person isn't able to pray effectively"
- **Greek:** *ou dynatai entynchanein* — is not able to intercede/pray
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the rich man cannot pray effectively" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). The Greek uses the intercession verb *entynchanō*; adding "effectively" clarifies that the issue is effectiveness, not capacity.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 51:7 "the prayer of the rich" vs. "the rich man's giving"

- **EMET:** "nor let the poor man think lightly of the prayer of the rich"
- **LOGOS:** "nor let the poor man despise the rich man's intercession on his behalf"
- **PNEUMA:** "let the poor person not underestimate the value of the rich person's generosity"
- **Greek:** *mēde ho plousios oligōrē tēn diakoníans* — nor let the rich one despise the ministry; but for poor: parallel structure
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "nor let the poor man despise the rich man's giving on his behalf." The poor man's side of the reciprocity involves not despising the economic ministry of the rich.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 51:7 "enriched by God" — treatment

- **EMET:** "the rich man is enriched by God"
- **LOGOS:** "the rich man is made rich before God"
- **PNEUMA:** "the rich person is enriched by God"
- **Greek:** *ho plousios ploutizestai hypo tou theou* — the rich one is made rich by God
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the rich man is enriched by God" (EMET/PNEUMA). "Enriched" captures the causative sense of *ploutizō* (to make rich); LOGOS's "before God" slightly changes the meaning.

---

## Disagreement 11 — 51:7 "perform their work" vs. "perform their respective tasks"

- **EMET:** "when they do their work"
- **LOGOS:** "when they perform their respective tasks"
- **PNEUMA:** "when each does what they're meant to do"
- **Greek:** *ta erga poiountes autōn* — doing their works/tasks
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "when they perform their respective tasks" (LOGOS). "Respective tasks" makes the mutuality explicit without adding interpretation.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 51.*
